history.title: Condominium History - Today
history.subtitle: Landmarks of Condominium Housing (1959 - Present)
history.y1959: Appointment of a committee to study housing issues of Sri Lanka.
history.y1963: Launching of the first policy statement on the housing policy of Sri Lanka.
history.y1970: Introduction of legal provisions as to a condominium property by the Condominium Property Act, No. 12 of 1970.
history.y1973: Apartment Ownership Act, No. 11 of 1973 was adopted so as to confer extensive powers for the management of multistory and apartment houses under the Ceiling on Housing Property Law, No. 01 of 1973. This repealed the Act, No. 12 of 1972 and introduced provisions making it lawful for the owners of units to form themselves into associations or bodies. Similarly, the Common Amenities Board was established by Act, No. 10 of 1973 for the maintenance of such properties.
history.y1982: Apartment Ownership Act, No.45 of 1982 introduced the system of Management Corporation and it contained provisions for the reinforcement of the system of Management Corporations.
history.y2003: The Common Amenities Board Act, No.10 of 1973 was amended by Act, No. 24 of 2003, facilitating the establishment of the Condominium Management Authority with wide ranging powers including the registration of the condominium plan and the declaration after the completion of the condominium property, issuing a certificate for common elements prior to such registration, regulating all activities of the Management Corporation formed after the registration of the property, settling issues amongst various stakeholders of the condominium property, removing unauthorized structures and redeveloping the property.
history.y2017: Gazette No: 2026/25 dated 05 July 2017 was issued incorporating details on the basic requirements to be fulfilled for the issuance of condominium certificate, conformities and charging of fees.
history.yToday: Today, the Condominium Management Authority (CMA) continues to regulate, manage, and facilitate modern condominium living in Sri Lanka, fostering sustainable, green, and high-quality urban development.

mc_powers.title: Powers of the Management Corporation
mc_powers.intro: Under the Condominium Property Act, every registered Management Corporation is vested with several corporate and executive legal powers to enforce by-laws and successfully manage common property amenities:
mc_powers.p01: To contract with the National Water Supply and Drainage Board, the Ceylon Electricity Board, any local authority or any other licensee for the supply of water, electricity and other utilities to condominium parcels of buildings.
mc_powers.p02: To take every step to recover the monthly charges for the consumption of water, electricity and other utilities provided by statutory bodies such as the National Water Supply and Drainage Board and the Ceylon Electricity Board by way of discontinuance of individual connections and to continue the discontinuance of such supply until the payment of respective charges.
mc_powers.p03: To purchase, hire or otherwise acquire movable property for use by the owners of all the units in connection with their enjoyment of the common elements.
mc_powers.p04: To pay rent, rates and insurance premia in relation to the control, management and administration of common elements.
mc_powers.p05: To levy a monthly contribution on the owners of all the condominium parcels in proportion to the share parcels of their respective condominium parcels for the purpose of discharging any obligation of the management corporation.
mc_powers.p06: To take decisions required for the discontinuance of services and utilities including water and electricity supplied through the management corporation of the condominium parcel owners who default such contributions.
mc_powers.p07: To borrow moneys with the consent of condominium parcel owners at a general meeting required by it in the exercise of its powers or the performance of its duties.
mc_powers.p08: To take steps necessary for the performance of its duties and for the enforcement of the by-laws set in the Second Schedule of the Apartment Ownership Act.
mc_powers.p09: To take steps for the removal of all unauthorized constructions constructed in violation of the certified building plan or make a request from a statutory body to have them removed.
mc_powers.p10: To inform the Condominium Management Authority in the event of the inability of parcel owners of the condominium property to duly maintain common amenities and common elements of the property.
mc_powers.p11: To make a request from the Condominium Management Authority to accept the responsibility of managing common elements and supplying common amenities until such time the parcel owners are in a position to manage common elements. (The Condominium Management Authority should perform this task only after a formal inquiry to ascertain whether the residents are in fact unable to perform this function.)
mc_powers.p12: To make and implement additional by-laws through the adoption of special resolutions at the meetings of the Management Corporation for the efficient management of common elements of the condominium property or the semi condominium property.
mc_powers.tool_desc: Select a common condominium management challenge below to see which legal powers the MC can utilize and what statutory options are available.
mc_powers.scenario1_tip: The MC can levy monthly contributions proportionally (Power 5). If a parcel owner defaults, the MC has the legal authority to discontinue supplied services and utilities such as electricity or water (Power 6).
mc_powers.scenario2_tip: The MC is legally empowered to take actions for the removal of all unauthorized constructions that violate the certified building plan, or formally request a statutory body to carry out the demolition (Power 9).
mc_powers.scenario3_tip: For major capital expenditures exceeding normal reserves, the MC has the power to borrow capital funds, provided they obtain majority consent from the parcel owners during a General Meeting (Power 7).
mc_powers.scenario4_title: 4. Utility Arrears on Shared Complex Bills
mc_powers.scenario4_tip: To prevent utility provider termination (NWSDB / CEB), the MC has the power to disconnect individual connections of defaulting owners and keep them suspended until arrears are cleared (Power 2).

mc_corporation.title: Management Corporation
mc_corporation.subtitle: Understanding the Legal Status, Permanence, and Role of the MC
mc_corporation.para1: The unit thus established collectively by unit owners for the maintenance, management and administration of their housing units is known as the Management Corporation. It is a corporation with legal powers and powers have been vested in the Management Corporation by the Apartment Ownership (Amendment) Act, No. 45 of 1982 to be involved in all activities in relation to the maintenance, management and administration of apartment complexes. Further, from the date any person becomes a housing unit or units of a condominium property, he or she automatically becomes a member of the management corporation.
mc_corporation.para2: According to the Apartment Ownership Act, No. 1 Of 1973; 'from the day an individual becomes an owner of a condominium parcel of a condominium property until the termination of condominium status of such property by an arbitrator appointed through a court order subsequent to the destruction of building or buildings of such property, the Management Corporation should remain in force'.
mc_corporation.para3: This underscores the importance of a Management Corporation remaining active until a condominium property is destroyed and redeveloped and the lifespan of a condominium property is determined by factors such as the construction technology, environmental changes, human activities, redevelopment stemming from urbanization. It is because the Management Corporation has the powers to deal with all issues of a condominium property.
mc_corporation.para4: However, the most pressing issue is that condominium property owners have still not understood the significance of actively maintaining a Management Corporation. This issue primarily prevails in government built apartment complexes the ownership of which has been transferred to owners. In the majority of condominium properties constructed by the private sector, the Management Corporations are in active operation and it appears that residents thereof have clearly understood the importance of the Management Corporation. Therefore a pleasant environment for living exists in such apartment such multi-storey complexes.
mc_corporation.lifecycle_subtitle: The four key stages of establishing and operating an MC under Sri Lankan law
mc_corporation.step1_desc: Obtain the Certificate of Conformity (CoC) from the local authority (Municipal Council/Pradeshiya Sabha) once construction is complete.
mc_corporation.step2_desc: Draft the certified Condominium Plan (Form B) showing unit boundaries, common elements, and share entitlement values.
mc_corporation.step3_desc: Submit the plan to the Registrar General and register the first Deed of Transfer. The MC is automatically incorporated on this day.
mc_corporation.step4_desc: Convene the First Annual General Meeting within 3 months to elect the Management Council (Chairperson, Secretary, Treasurer) and set funds.

mc_composition.title: Composition of the MC Official and Council
mc_composition.subtitle: Governance, Election & Quorum of the Executive Committee
mc_composition.intro: At a Annual General Meeting of the Management Corporation, an executive committee must be elected to carry out Administration, Maintenance & Management on behalf of all members who are entitled to membership in the Management Corporation. This executive body is referred to as the Committee (Board).
mc_composition.intro2: The committee is elected either unanimously or by a majority agreement of the condominium unit owners, according to their preference.
mc_composition.size_desc: The committee elected at a Annual General Meeting of the Management Corporation shall consist of a minimum of three (3) condominium unit owners and a maximum of fourteen (14) condominium unit owners. The term of official of the committee elected at each General Meeting shall expire at the next General Meeting.
mc_composition.quorum_desc: The quorum for a committee meeting shall be one-half of the total number of committee members. For example, if the committee consists of Six (6) members, the quorum shall be Three (3) members. If the committee consists of thirteen (13) or fourteen (14) members, the quorum shall be seven (7) members.
mc_composition.voting_desc: Decisions at committee meetings may be made by a simple majority vote.
mc_composition.election_desc: The committee is elected unanimously or by majority agreement of the condominium unit owners at the Annual General Meeting.
mc_composition.term_desc: The term of the committee elected at each General Meeting shall expire at the next General Meeting.
mc_composition.role_chair_desc: The principal executive officer. Presides over all council meetings, ensures by-laws are enforced, and coordinates all administrative tasks on behalf of the Management Corporation.
mc_composition.role_sec_desc: Maintains MC registers, updates council member records, files structural and financial certifications to the CMA, documents meeting minutes and handles all correspondence.
mc_composition.role_treas_desc: Oversees financial portfolios. Manages maintenance levy collections, sinking funds, and publishes audited accounts prior to the AGM.
mc_composition.enforcement_title: How the Council is Held Accountable
mc_composition.enforcement_desc: All members of the elected committee are accountable to the Management Corporation and its unit owners. Decisions must be made transparently, and financial records must be made available at every AGM.

mc_responsibilities.title: Responsibility of the Management Corporation
mc_responsibilities.subtitle: Statutory Duties and Mandates under the Condominium Property Act
mc_responsibilities.intro: The Management Corporation serves as the legal guardian of the vertical community. Under the Condominium Property Act, it is mandated to execute these core maintenance, financial, and regulatory duties:
mc_responsibilities.p01: Managing and properly maintaining the common elements and common amenities and keeping them in a state of good and serviceable repair to enable the parcel owners/occupants to obtain services thereof daily.
mc_responsibilities.p02: Effecting timely repairs necessary to common elements and common amenities of the building of the property by the Management Corporation.
mc_responsibilities.p03: Supplying common amenities as per the requirements of the residents and recovering charges for same.
mc_responsibilities.p04: Insuring and keeping insured the buildings in such property against loss or damage by fire, civil commotion, riot, and other hazards, and sharing the insurance premiums among all owners in proportion to their respective interest.
mc_responsibilities.p05: Applying forthwith insurance moneys received by it for damages caused to buildings or equipment for rebuilding and reinstating the same.
mc_responsibilities.p06: Preventing the construction of unauthorized structures in the condominium property, and requesting or assisting the Condominium Management Authority or any local authority to remove such structures.
mc_responsibilities.p07: Paying lease rent and assessment taxes in respect of the condominium property.
mc_responsibilities.p08: Stopping damages being caused to buildings or common elements.
mc_responsibilities.p09: Complying with any notice or order made by any public or statutory authority (such as the CMA or a local government authority) requiring the abatement of any nuisance on the common elements or ordering repairs if a unit owner has failed to comply, and recovering the costs thereof from the condominium parcel owners.
mc_responsibilities.tool_desc: Select a responsibility domain below to filter and view the exact statutory duties mandated under Sri Lankan law.
mc_responsibilities.enforcement_desc: Under Section 20 of the Condominium Property Act, failure of a Management Corporation to execute these statutory duties can result in intervention by the CMA, including appointed management or legal penalties.

mc_living_habits.title: Condominium Living Habits
mc_living_habits.subtitle: Code of Conduct and Best Practices Expected from Unit Owners
mc_living_habits.intro: Living in a condominium demands mutual respect, cooperation, and good civic habits. Adhering to these neighborly etiquettes maintains peace, avoids disputes, and makes the condominium a pleasant home for everyone.
mc_living_habits.p01: Epidemiological diseases have been found to be prevalent in condominium properties. The carelessness of any resident in one unit can make all the residents suffer from diseases.
mc_living_habits.p02: It has been found that air pollution associated with houses is more serious than ambient air pollution. The effects of air pollution in one house can affect the neighboring houses as well.
mc_living_habits.p03: Non-permission of unauthorized constructions to cover not only public facilities but in some cases even paths laid to prevent the spread of fire or escape in case of fire.
mc_living_habits.p04: Large billboards should not be installed to block ventilation.
mc_living_habits.p05: Making sure not to create an environment where insects breed inside the home and in confined spaces.
mc_living_habits.p06: Avoid collecting things that spread odors.
mc_living_habits.p07: Use of proper garbage disposal methods.
mc_living_habits.p09: Behaving and conducting one's business so as not to disturb others.
mc_living_habits.p10: Being sensitive to the needs and wants of others.
mc_living_habits.p11: Make sure to be friendly with others.
mc_living_habits.p13: Willingness to limit one's desires for the common good.

mc_unit_owner.title: Unit Owners' Responsibility
mc_unit_owner.subtitle: Statutory Duties and Obligations of Condominium Unit Owners
mc_unit_owner.intro: Living in a condominium involves shared foundations and mutual community living. Under the Condominium Property Act, individual unit owners carry specific legal obligations to protect the safety, hygiene, and harmony of all residents.
mc_unit_owner.p01: Do not use the unit for any illegal, unlawful, or unauthorized purpose that could bring disrepute or harm the reputation of the building.
mc_unit_owner.p02: Do not use any material, substance, or fuel that generates excessive smoke, noxious fumes, or offensive odors within the unit.
mc_unit_owner.p03: Do not throw, dump, or allow refuse, rubbish, or garbage to fall onto common elements, common areas, or balconies, except in bins provided for the unit or the building.
mc_unit_owner.p04: Do not keep any pet or animal in the unit or common elements that could cause annoyance, nuisance, or disturbance to other unit owners.
mc_unit_owner.p05: Do not use or permit the unit to be used in any manner or for any purpose that causes nuisance, harassment, or a hazardous condition to other owners or their families.
mc_unit_owner.p06: Provide full, active cooperation to the Management Corporation to ensure proper administration, maintenance, and management of common elements.
mc_unit_owner.p07: Permit the Management Corporation and its representatives to enter the unit at all reasonable times, after reasonable notice (except in emergencies when notice is not required), for these tasks:
mc_unit_owner.p07_sub1: To inspect the condition of the unit.
mc_unit_owner.p07_sub2: To repair, maintain, or renew pipes, sewers, wires, cables, or ducts used or capable of being used for other units or common areas.
mc_unit_owner.p07_sub3: To maintain or renew common elements.
mc_unit_owner.p07_sub4: To carry out any work necessary to enforce building by-laws or execute corporation duties.
mc_unit_owner.p08: Promptly execute all repairs or work required by any government, public, or statutory authority in respect of the unit (excluding work for the general benefit of the building), and pay all assessments and rates on time.
mc_unit_owner.p09: Properly repair and maintain the unit, keeping it in a clean and safe condition, fair wear and tear and damage by fire, storm, tempest, or act of God excepted.
mc_unit_owner.p10: Use and enjoy the common elements in a manner that does not obstruct, interfere with, or adversely affect the lawful rights, use, and enjoyment of other residents and guests.
mc_unit_owner.p11: Do not use the unit for any purpose that violates the terms of use, zoning, or specifications outlined in the plans approved by the relevant authority.
mc_unit_owner.p12: Promptly notify the Management Corporation of any change in ownership, tenancy, or other transaction affecting the unit.

about_cert.title: Condominium Certification Stages
about_cert.subtitle: Understanding the three main stages of official property certification issued by the CMA.

provisional.title: Provisional Condominium Certificate
provisional.description: Issued at the initial stages of construction. This certificate enables developers to obtain bank loans and facilitates loan facilities for buyers purchasing units in the property.

semi.title: Semi Condominium Certificate
semi.description: Obtained when a specific portion or phase of the condominium property is completed while the rest is under development. It can be used for completed towers or a set of units.

full.title: Fully Condominium Certificate
full.description: Issued after the complete construction of the building in accordance with the approved building plan, ensuring there are no unauthorized constructions. A mandatory certificate for complete legal compliance.

about_cert.ready_desc: You can apply and download your official condominium certificates directly through our secure online portal. Log in to your citizen account to begin.
